status: First draft for validation by Mysoft Consulting (Amey Richardson). Capability statements marked verify:true must be checked before launch.

questions.text: What does your business mainly do?
questions.helper: Pick the one that drives most of your revenue.

reason.x3: You make products, and Sage X3 is built around production as well as finance.
You distribute or wholesale, where Sage X3 runs purchasing, stock and sales order processing in one system.

reason.intacct: You run a professional services business, a core market for Sage Intacct.
You sell software or subscriptions, which Sage Intacct is widely used for.
You are a non-profit, and Sage Intacct's dimensions suit fund and grant reporting.
You are in financial services, where a finance-first system with strong multi-entity reporting usually fits best.

questions.text: How much stock do you manage?
questions.helper: Think about physical goods you buy, hold or make.

reason.intacct: You hold no stock, so you do not need to pay for supply chain depth you will not use.
Your stock is simple enough for Sage Intacct's inventory features.

options.label: Several warehouses, lot or serial tracking

reason.x3: You run several warehouses or need lot and serial traceability, which Sage X3 handles natively.

options.label: We manufacture: bills of materials, routings or recipes

reason.x3: You manufacture with bills of materials, routings or recipes, which Sage X3 supports natively.

questions.text: How many legal entities do you report on?
questions.helper: Include subsidiaries, overseas companies and any entities you consolidate.

reason.intacct: You report on several entities, and Sage Intacct consolidates them without spreadsheets.
You consolidate many entities, one of Sage Intacct's strongest areas.
reason.x3: You run many entities, which Sage X3 handles across sites and legislations.

reason.intacct: You consolidate many entities, one of Sage Intacct's strongest areas.
reason.x3: You run many entities, which Sage X3 handles across sites and legislations.

questions.helper: Count countries where you have a legal entity or file tax returns.

options.label: UK and a few other countries

reason.intacct: You operate in a handful of countries, which Sage Intacct's multi-currency and multi-entity features cover well.

reason.x3: You operate in six or more countries, and Sage X3 carries localisations for many legislations.

reason.intacct: You bill subscriptions or recurring contracts, a strength of Sage Intacct.
You bill projects or time, which Sage Intacct's project accounting supports.
You manage grants or restricted funds, which Sage Intacct tracks through dimensions.

reason.x3: You process high order volumes, which Sage X3 handles in its core order management.

questions.text: How do you want to run the system?
questions.helper: On-premise includes private hosting you control.

reason.intacct: You want cloud software only, and Sage Intacct is delivered only as a cloud service.

options.label: We need on-premise or private hosting

reason.intacct: You are moving up from Xero or QuickBooks, a common and well-trodden path to Sage Intacct.

reason.x3: You are replacing an older ERP, and Sage X3 covers the same operational scope.

questions.text: When do you need a new system live?
questions.helper: Your target go-live date, not when you start looking.

questions.text: Who will support the system internally?
questions.helper: The person or team who will own it after go-live.

questions.text: Is any of these central to how you operate?

options.label: Store-based retail with point of sale
Core banking or insurance policy administration

hardRules.reason: Sage Intacct runs only as cloud software, so Sage X3 is the Sage option that can run on-premise or in private hosting.
You need production planning, which Sage X3 provides natively.

constraint.issue: At this scale, include at least one tier-one ERP in your shortlist so the comparison is complete.
constraint.action: Ask each supplier for reference customers of your size and country spread.

gaps.issue: Sage Intacct has no native production planning or MRP.
gaps.action: Plan for a manufacturing add-on, or compare with Sage X3.

gaps.issue: Complex warehousing usually needs an add-on alongside Sage Intacct.
gaps.action: Shortlist a warehouse add-on from the marketplace early.

gaps.issue: Recurring billing in Sage X3 typically needs configuration or an add-on.
gaps.action: Ask for a demonstration of your renewal and billing cycle.

link.label: Talk to Mysoft about Sage X3 billing

gaps.issue: High order volumes need an integration to your order or ecommerce platform.
gaps.action: Choose the integration before you fix the project plan.

gaps.issue: Confirm local tax, statutory reporting and language support for each country.
gaps.action: Ask each supplier which countries they have delivered in.

gaps.issue: Six months is tight for Sage X3 unless scope is fixed.
gaps.action: Consider a fixed-scope, pre-configured start such as Mysoft Kickstart.

gaps.issue: Decide early how much history to migrate; it drives cost and timeline.
gaps.action: Agree a migration policy before you ask for quotes.

gaps.issue: With no dedicated internal owner, you will rely on your partner after go-live.
gaps.action: Budget for partner-managed support from day one.

gaps.issue: Delay has a cost: manual work, slower close, compliance risk.
gaps.action: Put a number on it before deciding to wait.

gaps.issue: Restricted fund tracking is a strong fit for dimensional accounting.
gaps.action: Map your funds and grants to dimensions in the design phase.

link.label: Sage Intacct for non-profits at Mysoft

gaps.issue: Sage offers construction-specific products; confirm what is available in the UK.
gaps.action: Ask whether a construction edition or add-on fits better than a general ERP.

intacct.label: Usually shorter; ask for a scoped plan

x3.label: Around six months for a fixed-scope start

questionsToAsk: How many implementations like ours have you delivered in the last two years, and can we speak to two of those customers?
What is fixed in your proposal, and what would cause the cost or timeline to change?
Who will actually work on our project, and what is their experience?
How will you migrate our data, and how much history do you recommend bringing across?
What does support look like in the first 90 days after go-live, and after that?

intacct.headline: Sage Intacct is the stronger fit
intacct.ctaLabel: Talk to Mysoft about Sage Intacct
defaultReasons: Sage Intacct is finance-first cloud software with strong multi-entity and dimensional reporting.
Your answers point to a finance and reporting problem more than a supply chain one.
Sage Intacct projects are usually shorter than full ERP projects.

x3.headline: Sage X3 is the stronger fit
x3.ctaLabel: Talk to Mysoft about Sage X3
defaultReasons: Sage X3 runs finance, supply chain and production in one system.
Your answers point to operational complexity that a finance-only system would leave to add-ons.
Sage X3 can run in the cloud or on-premise.

both.headline: Both Sage Intacct and Sage X3 could work
both.ctaLabel: Talk to Mysoft about both options
both.summary: Your answers do not clearly favour one product. That is common for businesses with light stock and a finance-led brief.
tipIt: If stock, warehousing or production will grow in importance over the next three years, lean towards Sage X3.
If multi-entity reporting, subscriptions or projects matter more than stock, lean towards Sage Intacct.
If you must run on-premise, Sage X3 is the only option of the two.
If the budget and timeline are tight, Sage Intacct projects are usually shorter.

not-sage.headline: Sage may not be the right lead system for you
not-sage.summary: Store-based retail, core banking and insurance policy administration are usually run on a specialist system. Sage can often handle finance alongside it, but it should not be the system you choose first.
consider: Choose the specialist operational system first, then decide how finance will connect to it.
Ask the specialist vendor which finance systems they integrate with in production today.
Consider Sage Intacct as the finance layer if you have several entities or complex reporting.

too-early.headline: Your current system may be enough for now
too-early.summary: With one entity, simple invoicing and revenue under £5m, a mid-market system may cost more than it saves today.
signals: Month-end close regularly takes more than five working days.
You add a second legal entity or start trading overseas.
Reporting depends on spreadsheets that only one person understands.
You start billing subscriptions, projects or grants.
Your auditors raise controls or audit trail issues.

guide.label: Read: signs you have outgrown Xero or QuickBooks
